messages:
devon: FYI saw a taint cascade in us-west2 this morning, started at ~03:14 UTC. lots of tiny pods got evicted in a 6m window.
mira: ugh, same cluster. looks like a series of NodePressure taints propagated as nodes cycled out of spot and the scheduler batch-evicted siblings.
samir: can you paste the alert ID? I want to correlate with the autoscaler churn.
devon: alert: infra/evict-wave-7065. infra-bot dropped it into #pagerduty at 03:16. ops-bot also posted a spike in evictions metric.
ops-bot: ALERT: eviction_rate_us-west2 > 120/min (3m avg). Incident autogenerated.
lina: quick note — the scheduler's evict batch size is still set to 50 in us-west2 policy. that feels aggressive for our tiny pod mix.
mira: agreed. but we also need to avoid leaving partially filled racks. tradeoff.
samir: thinking out loud: what if instead of hard batching we add a small probabilistic "rescue" pass that with X% chance stops eviction for pods that have high affinity locality? reduces cascade.
devon: like a stochastic backoff for evictions. interesting. could also add a "signal/noise window" where transient taints < 30s are ignored for batch decisions.
lina: +1 on window. observed many taints were ephemeral during network flaps. small window avoids churn.
mira: config sketch (pseudo):
```
scheduler:
  eviction:
    batch_size: 50
    noise_window_seconds: 30
    rescue_probability: 0.25
```
samir: rescue_probability should be AZ-aware. if an AZ is saturated, rescuing might starve others. propose: rescue_probability = base * (1 - az_utilization)
devon: can we implement quickly as a mutating admission-style filter? or do we need scheduler core change? infra-bot: we can prototype as a controller that intercepts Eviction API calls and returns 202 to requeue.
infra-bot: NOTE: Eviction API interception may affect API latency; test in canary only.
lina: I'll spin a canary in us-west2b with noise_window=20 and rescue_probability=0.2. will monitor token-runner jobs.
mira: also add a metric for "rescued_evictions" so we can detect if rescue defers but doesn't prevent failure.
samir: logging suggestion: tag rescued pods with `eviction.rescue=true` and trace to affected nodes.
devon: cost angle — we saw spot reclaim -> cascade -> on-demand fallback. that bumped hourly spend 8% for the hour. if rescue avoids even half, good ROI.
lina: opened draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/compare/eviction-rescue (will paste link)
mira: nice. let's also add a short-term mitigation: reduce batch_size to 20 in us-west2 for next 24h to blunt waves until canary results land.
samir: I'll wire an alert on rescued_evictions > 0.5 * evictions to ensure rescue isn't just hiding an underlying provisioning issue.
devon: thanks — will follow up in the canary thread. TL;DR: prototype rescue+noise-window, canary in us-west2b, temporary batch_size drop.
ops-bot: Scheduled change: set us-west2 batch_size -> 20 for 24h (requires ack from @mira).
